 2   Q.   Please state your name and business address.

 1                        SELECTION AND MANAGEMENT OF MAJOR PROJECTS

 2                   Description of the Major Projects Group
 3   Q.      Please describe the Major Projects Group and the work that it performs to

 4           support SPS’s operations.

 5   A.      The Major Projects Group is a multi-regional organization within Xcel Energy

 6           Services that manages large, complex, capital projects for all Xcel Energy

 7           Operating Companies, including SPS. 2                 The group oversees the planning,

 8           engineering, procurement, and construction of new electric generating facilities and

 9           major generation upgrades. Through this work, the Major Projects Group supports

10           SPS’s ability to produce and deliver reliable electricity to the homes and businesses

11           of its New Mexico retail customers.

12   Q.      What types of projects are included in the Major Projects Group?

13   A.      The Major Projects Group manages SPS’s largest capital investments, typically

14           projects exceeding $100 million in total cost or involving significant engineering

15           complexity. These projects include new generating facilities, major plant retrofits,

 3   Q.   Does the Major Projects Group include smaller business units or groups?

 4   A.   No.

 5   Q.   What are the primary business drivers affecting the Major Project capital

 6        expenditures?

 7   A.   Multiple factors influence the Major Project capital requirements. SPS’s capital

 8        needs have increased because of unprecedented load growth in SPS’s service

 9        territory, the construction of new energy renewable resources to meet state clean

10        energy targets, installation of grid stabilizing technologies on SPS’s system, and

11        the conversion of generating technologies at existing power plants. In addition,

12        SPS’s capital investment is impacted by the age of SPS’s units, their proximity to

13        retirement, and SPS’s operations within the Southwest Power Pool.

 1               Selection Process for Major Projects
 2   Q.   How does SPS identify and select Major Projects?

 3   A.   SPS’s selection of Major Projects begins with its Integrated Resource Plan (“IRP”)

 4        and competitive Request for Proposals (“RFP”) process. Through that process, SPS

 5        solicits and evaluates bids for self-build and third-party generation projects that best

 6        meet system needs. For SPS-owned or operated generation projects, SPS seeks

 7        CCNs before the Commission. Once SPS obtains a CCN for a major capital

 8        project, it records the project into its financial capital plan and includes the project

 9        in its ratemaking forecasts.

10                Major Project Costs
11   Q.   How does the Major Projects Group develop cost estimates for proposed

12        capital additions?

13   A.   Projects are identified and evaluated by Integrated System Planning, an

14        organization within Xcel Energy specifically tasked with coordinating modeling

15        and planning of needed generation, transmission, and distribution projects to best

16        serve its four operating companies, including SPS. During this process, a scope of

17        work and preliminary engineering is completed to allow an estimate to be made for

18        the project. Projects are evaluated and selected for inclusion as a response for

 1        Request for Proposal. Contingency is included at this point to address the risk

 2        identified for the project. A project is reviewed and approved prior to submission

 3        into the RFP process.

 4   Q.   Does the Major Projects Group have a process to help manage capital costs?

 5   A.   Yes. As I explained earlier, a capital project is assigned to a project manager after

 6        it has been approved for execution, with that assignment typically occurring three

 7        to six months in advance of the first activity required to commence the project.

 8        That gives the project manager time to work with the plant engineering and

 9        technical services personnel and other subject matter experts to review and more

10        fully develop the final scope, schedule, and monthly cash flow requirements for the

11        assigned project. As part of that process, the project manager is expected to identify

12        opportunities to control capital costs.

13   Q.   Is it typical for the Major Projects Group to use competitive bidding to manage

14        capital costs?

15   A.   Yes. When feasible, the project manager solicits competitive bids for the project

16        work by working with the Xcel Energy Supply Chain organization to firm up cost

17        and schedule data during the engineering and purchasing activities.

 1   Q.   Is it possible for the budgeted capital expenditures to change during the

 2        planning process or after the project is underway?

 3   A.   Yes. After a project is funded and begins, the project manager receives weekly or

 4        monthly reports that track actual expenditures and compares such expenditures to

 5        the capital budget for the project. Each month, significant budget variances are

 6        noted and reviewed to determine the cause for the variance and to identify

 7        corrective actions that can be taken. If corrective action is necessary and feasible,

 8        it is implemented. At times, the variance is simply a timing issue and no corrective

 9        action is necessary.

10                 In other cases, the budget may need to be amended because the project is

11        more or less costly than originally contemplated. In such situations, a scope or

12        budget change order is developed that revises the project to align with the current

13        needs.

 1   Q.      How are capital project costs captured in the Xcel Energy accounting system?

 2   A.      SPS uses what it calls a Work Breakdown Structure (“WBS”), which Ms. Kietzman

 3           discusses in more detail in her direct testimony. Generally speaking, overall capital

 4           projects are recorded at WBS Level 1, whereas sub-projects within the overall

 5           project are recorded at lower WBS Level 2, WBS Level 3, or WBS Level 4. 3

 6   Q.      Is a capital WBS Level 4 order closed as soon as the equipment subject to that

 7           order is placed in service?

 8   A.      No. Frequently, minor work continues after the equipment is placed in service, and

 9           charges can continue for a short period after the in-service date is recognized on a

10           WBS Level 4 order. These charges can include recognition of the final bills from

11           vendors, testing of the equipment, and settlement of any disputes.

 1   Q.   Please describe the major categories of SPS’s Major Project investments.

 2   A.   SPS groups its production capital investments into three categories: (1) Reliability

 3        and Performance Enhancement, (2) Environmental Compliance, and (3) New

 4        Generation. Each category identifies the primary purpose of the investment and

 5        mirrors how SPS classifies major projects in its capital planning process.

 6   Q.   What types of projects are included in the Reliability and Performance

 7        Enhancement category?

 8   A.   This category includes capital additions that maintain and improve the safety,

 9        performance, and reliability of SPS’s generating units. These projects prevent

10        unplanned outages, sustain a high reliability factor, and ensure safe working

11        conditions that meet all applicable standards. Typical work includes turbine

12        inspections, component overhauls, boiler tube replacements, and other work needed

13        to sustain dependable generation.

4         and state environmental regulations and permit conditions. These investments

 5        allow SPS’s facilities to operate lawfully and without interruption. Typical work

 6        includes replacing wastewater recovery systems, refurbishing evaporation ponds,

 7        improving landfills, and upgrading pollution control-equipment.

 8   Q.   What types of projects are included in New Generation category?

 9   A.   This category of investment includes the capital additions necessary to place new

10        generation in service. These additions expand SPS’s capacity, improve system

11        flexibility, and help meet future customer demand.
